title: audit-log-exporter: wire private installer sinks, retention config, and Helm values
author: Priya Raman
description: Context: Private deployments must export audit logs reliably to customer-configurable sinks and meet retention/compliance requirements. The existing audit-log-exporter chart was only wired for hosted defaults; this PR wires exporter into the private installer and Helm overlays, exposes retention/KMS/sink configuration via Terraform variables and Helm values, and adds upgrade/rollback safety checks. Motivation: enterprise customers deploying Redwood Private require auditable exports (syslog/HTTPS/S3) with configurable retention and KMS-backed encryption. This change reduces manual post-install steps and ensures audit trails survive upgrades. What this PR does: 1) Installer wiring - plumbs audit-log-exporter as an optional service in the private installer (redwood-private-installer) with template-driven values for VPC endpoints, networkPolicies, and serviceAccounts. 2) Helm chart updates - adds values.auditExporter.enabled, values.auditExporter.retentionDays, values.auditExporter.sink.* (s3, https, syslog), and values.auditExporter.kmsKeyId. Includes chart hooks for graceful pre-upgrade drain and post-upgrade verification. 3) Terraform module - exposes audit exporter config in terraform/redwood-terraform/modules/private (variables: audit_exporter_enabled, sink_type, s3_bucket, https_endpoint, syslog_host, retention_days, kms_key_arn). Adds outputs for rendered Helm values used by the installer. 4) Migration UX - adds a migration job (pre-upgrade) that validates sink connectivity and warns on retention reductions. 5) RBAC & security - tightens ServiceAccount permissions and documents required KMS IAM bindings. 6) Tests & CI - adds integration test that deploys installer to a local Kind cluster with a mocked S3 sink and asserts exported records. Checklist: - [x] Helm values and README updated - [x] Terraform variables and examples added - [x] Installer templates wired - [x] Migration warnings implemented - [x] Integration test added - [x] Alerts/metrics for exporter success/failure added Files changed (high level): - redwood-private-installer/templates/audit-log-exporter-deployment.yaml: add wiring, network policy annotations - charts/audit-log-exporter/values.schema.json & values.yaml: new fields and schema validation - terraform/modules/private/audit_exporter.tf: new variables/outputs and example usage - charts/audit-log-exporter/templates/hooks.yaml: pre-upgrade hook to drain exporter and post-upgrade verification job - charts/audit-log-exporter/templates/configmap.yaml: retention config and KMS reference - infra/scripts/migrations/audit-exporter-validate.sh: migration check used by installer - tests/integration/audit_exporter_e2e_test.go: Kind-based integration test (mock S3) Migrations and safety: - New Helm hook ensures exporter is drained before upgrade to avoid double-delivery. - Migration job will refuse to apply if retention_days is being reduced below existing retention unless --force is provided by operator. - Terraform changes are additive; default is disabled to avoid surprise enabling in existing deployments Documentation: updated private-installer/README.md with examples for S3/HTTPS/Syslog sinks, example IAM policies for KMS, and a troubleshooting section for common connectivity errors CI: added an integration stage that runs the new Kind test and a small e2e verification; CI is green on this branch but the Kind test was flaky on first run and retried once. Related: ENG-2034 (audit logging compliance), PM-412 (private installer GA checklist).
